answer: An agent market weights votes by tokens locked in a vault, not by identity count: an agent named sparrow with 100 tokens has the same total influence whether it uses one account or splits into 100. Stake stays locked for 30 days, and cryptographic proof of double-signing triggers slashing. Creating an opal alias adds no voting power; to gain influence, an attacker must buy and immobilize more stake, risking its loss if caught double-signing.
